name: Non-24-Hour Sleep-Wake Syndrome

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: International Classification of Sleep Disorders, 3rd Edition (ICSD-3)

criteria.description: Chronic pattern of sleep-wake cycle that is not aligned with the 24-hour day, showing a free-running circadian rhythm
Sleep diary or actigraphy demonstrating a consistent daily delay in sleep onset and wake times over at least 14 days
Exclusion of other sleep disorders, medical, neurological, or psychiatric conditions that could explain the symptoms
Symptoms present for at least 3 months

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of chronic free-running circadian rhythm confirmed by sleep logs or actigraphy, with exclusion of other causes
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis often requires longitudinal monitoring due to variability in symptom expression.

searchTerms: feeling very sleepy during the day
abnormal melatonin levels from pineal gland

genetic: Mutations or polymorphisms in circadian clock genes (e.g., CLOCK, PER3) have been implicated in some cases
other: Actigraphy and sleep diaries showing non-24-hour sleep-wake patterns
Melatonin rhythm assays demonstrating free-running circadian phase

distinguishingFeatures: Sleep onset delayed but remains entrained to 24-hour cycle
Stable sleep-wake times with delayed phase rather than free-running
Highly fragmented sleep without a clear circadian pattern
No progressive daily delay in sleep onset

redFlags: Sudden onset of circadian rhythm disruption
Presence of neurological deficits or cognitive decline
Signs of psychiatric disorders requiring urgent intervention
references: American Academy of Sleep Medicine. International Classification of Sleep Disorders, 3rd Edition. 2014.
Lockley SW, Skene DJ, Arendt J. Circadian rhythm sleep disorders: Part I, basic principles, shift work and jet lag disorders. Sleep Med Rev. 2007.
Sack RL, et al. Circadian rhythm sleep disorders: Part II, advanced sleep phase disorder, delayed sleep phase disorder, free-running disorder, and irregular sleep-wake rhythm. Sleep. 2007.
